study_name: Meno-J Theory Study 1: What Makes an Explanation Genuinely Good?
research_question: What properties distinguish a genuinely good explanation from a merely accurate, detailed, simple, persuasive, or predictive account?

method.qualification: This is a defensible architecture synthesis, not an empirical proof or a priority claim of philosophical novelty.

sources.authors: Carl G. Hempel and Paul Oppenheim
sources.title: Studies in the Logic of Explanation
sources.contribution: Makes explanation auditable through derivation from laws and initial conditions, with truth and law-likeness requirements.
sources.pressure_point: Formal derivability does not by itself secure direction, relevance, or immunity from spurious regularities.

sources.title: Explanatory Unification and the Causal Structure of the World
sources.contribution: Explains why a small number of argument patterns that derive many facts can increase understanding.
sources.pressure_point: Unification can impose a false unity on heterogeneous mechanisms and can reward a compact but wrong system.

sources.title: Scientific Explanation: Causation and Unification
sources.contribution: Treats causal-mechanical and unification accounts as potentially complementary rather than forced alternatives.
sources.pressure_point: Causal detail alone does not select the factors relevant to the contrast actually being asked about.

sources.authors: Peter Machamer, Lindley Darden, and Carl F. Craver
sources.title: Thinking About Mechanisms
sources.contribution: Characterizes mechanisms through organized entities and activities producing regular changes from start to finish.
sources.pressure_point: Mechanistic completeness may add enormous detail without identifying the difference-maker for a particular question.

sources.title: Making Things Happen: A Theory of Causal Explanation
sources.contribution: Connects causal explanation to invariant relations that answer what-if-things-had-been-different questions under interventions.
sources.pressure_point: Interventionism is strongest for causal explanation and should not be silently extended to mathematical, constitutive, or grounding explanation.

sources.title: The Scientific Image
sources.contribution: Shows that why-questions are contrastive and context-sensitive: why P rather than which alternative matters.
sources.pressure_point: Context may select a relevant valid answer, but cannot turn a false dependency or unsupported story into a good explanation.

sources.title: What Makes a Scientific Explanation Distinctively Mathematical?
sources.contribution: Establishes that some scientific explanations work through mathematical constraints rather than causal histories.
sources.pressure_point: A causal-only architecture will misclassify genuine constraint explanations.

sources.title: Is There a Monist Theory of Causal and Noncausal Explanations?
sources.contribution: Develops a unified counterfactual account intended to cover causal and noncausal explanation.
sources.pressure_point: The account faces overgeneration, directionality, necessary-truth, grounding, and overdetermination cases.

sources.title: Understanding as Compression
sources.contribution: Models understanding as a minimal representational kernel plus processes that regenerate useful information.
sources.pressure_point: Compression concerns an epistemic achievement and does not by itself guarantee truth, direction, or explanatory relevance.

sources.title: Metaphysical Explanations and the Counterfactual Theory of Explanation
sources.contribution: Tests a counterfactual monism against grounding, redundancy, overdetermination, and relevance cases.
sources.pressure_point: Weak dependency conditions trivialize; strong conditions exclude paradigmatic grounding explanations.

sources.title: Explanatory Pluralism and the (Dis)unity of Science
sources.contribution: Shows that explanations may resist integration when they imply incompatible counterfactual consequences.
sources.pressure_point: Pluralism needs a rule for genuine complementarity versus incompatible claims; otherwise it becomes anything-goes.

sources.title: A Roadmap to Explanatory Pluralism
sources.contribution: Separates type, fragmentation, and insular forms of explanatory pluralism.
sources.pressure_point: Saying that there are many explanation types is a map of the problem, not yet a quality-control procedure.

sources.authors: J. De Rizzo and B. Schnieder
sources.title: Mathematical Explanation: A Defence and a Challenge
sources.contribution: Defends mathematical explanation while arguing that ordinary counterfactual dependence is neither sufficient nor necessary for explanation.
sources.pressure_point: A universal counterfactual-compression definition fails mutual-dependence, overdetermination, constitution, and necessary-truth cases.

theory_matrix.name: Deductive-nomological
theory_matrix.best_insight: Good explanations must expose an inferential bridge and cannot be mere assertions.
theory_matrix.decisive_limit: Entailment plus true premises can preserve the wrong direction or irrelevant information.

theory_matrix.name: Unification
theory_matrix.best_insight: Explanatory breadth and reusable patterns matter; isolated restatement is weak.
theory_matrix.decisive_limit: A compact conspiracy or an imposed universal pattern can unify while tracking no warranted relation.

theory_matrix.name: Causal-mechanistic
theory_matrix.best_insight: Organized entities, activities, and causal direction distinguish productive stories from correlations.
theory_matrix.decisive_limit: Not every explanation is causal, and exhaustive mechanism can obscure the relevant difference-maker.

theory_matrix.name: Interventionist and counterfactual
theory_matrix.best_insight: A deep causal explanation supports stable what-if answers and identifies manipulable difference-makers.
theory_matrix.decisive_limit: Ordinary counterfactual dependence is neither universally necessary nor sufficient, especially under overdetermination and noncausal explanation.

theory_matrix.name: Pragmatic and contrastive
theory_matrix.best_insight: The same fact can answer one why-question and fail another because the foil and purpose differ.
theory_matrix.decisive_limit: Audience satisfaction cannot license falsehood or unsupported dependence.

theory_matrix.name: Mathematical and constraint-based
theory_matrix.best_insight: Necessity, impossibility, constitution, and grounding can explain without a causal process.
theory_matrix.decisive_limit: A proof that establishes a result need not reveal why it holds; type-specific direction and relevance still matter.

theory_matrix.name: Understanding as compression
theory_matrix.best_insight: Useful understanding removes detail while retaining the ability to regenerate needed information.
theory_matrix.decisive_limit: Compression can be achieved by an inaccurate, conspiratorial, or directionless representation.

theory_matrix.name: Explanatory pluralism
theory_matrix.best_insight: Different questions legitimately require different explanatory relation types and levels.
theory_matrix.decisive_limit: Incompatible consequences within the same target, contrast, and scope cannot all be accepted as complementary.

stress_tests.name: Flagpole and shadow reversal
stress_tests.challenge: A derivation can calculate pole height from shadow length although the shadow does not explain the pole.
stress_tests.contract_response: Require a type-specific direction warrant; for causal claims, interventions on pole height change the shadow, not conversely.

stress_tests.name: Barometer and storm
stress_tests.challenge: A barometer predicts a storm through a shared cause but does not cause or mechanically explain it.
stress_tests.contract_response: Require rivals and a causal/mechanistic warrant that distinguishes indicator, common cause, and producer.

stress_tests.name: Causal overdetermination
stress_tests.challenge: Bob's shot can explain a death even when Boba's shot would have caused death anyway, so simple but-for dependence fails.
stress_tests.contract_response: Allow causal-production and contribution warrants; record redundancy and test component-removal or timing consequences rather than only but-for dependence.

stress_tests.name: Scarlet and red constitution
stress_tests.challenge: Being scarlet can explain being red even though a nearby non-scarlet state may still be red.
stress_tests.contract_response: Route constitutive claims through asymmetric inclusion or grounding rather than an intervention test.

stress_tests.name: Königsberg bridges
stress_tests.challenge: The impossibility of an Eulerian walk is explained by graph structure, not by a causal history.
stress_tests.contract_response: Route mathematical claims through constraint, invariance, or impossibility derivations and test whether the cited structure is indispensable.

stress_tests.name: Perfect lookup table
stress_tests.challenge: A table can predict every observed case while supplying no transferable relation or answer to a changed case.
stress_tests.contract_response: Require generativity beyond stored instances and a warranted bridge from selected factors to the target.

stress_tests.name: Elegant conspiracy
stress_tests.challenge: A single hidden-agent story can compress and unify many facts while remaining insulated from failure.
stress_tests.contract_response: Validity, rival discrimination, and explicit failure conditions are mandatory gates that elegance cannot compensate for.

stress_tests.name: Mechanistic overload
stress_tests.challenge: A complete molecular history may be true but worse than a dose difference for explaining why this patient, rather than a matched patient, responded.
stress_tests.contract_response: Index relevance to the foil and require an irrelevance justification for omitted and included detail.

stress_tests.name: Foil shift
stress_tests.challenge: Why the plant died rather than lived, rather than the neighboring plant, and rather than yesterday are different questions.
stress_tests.contract_response: Require target, contrast, background, purpose, and scope before evaluating an answer.

stress_tests.name: Incompatible plural explanations
stress_tests.challenge: Two accounts may be useful at different levels yet imply incompatible consequences for the same intervention and scope.
stress_tests.contract_response: Treat accounts as complementary only when question or relation type differs; same-scope divergent consequences trigger a rival test.

failed_initial_candidate.name: Counterfactual Compression Theory
failed_initial_candidate.claim: A good explanation is a lossy compression that preserves counterfactual dependency structure.
why: Compression is not sufficient: false or unfalsifiable stories can compress and unify.
Ordinary counterfactual dependence is not sufficient: mutual or self-dependence can be nonexplanatory.
Ordinary counterfactual dependence is not necessary: overdetermined causal, constitutive, grounding, and some mathematical cases survive without it.
Understanding and explanation are related but not identical; a useful representation can be inaccurate.
failed_initial_candidate.scientific_value: The rejected candidate exposed the need for relation-type routing rather than a seductive monist slogan.

result.name: Meno-J Explanation Contract
result.short_definition: A good explanation is a question-indexed, selectively simplified account whose premises are adequately warranted, whose bridge to the target is licensed by the relevant relation type, and whose scope, rivals, consequences, omissions, and failure conditions are explicit.
not_claimed: a universal metaphysical essence of explanation
that counterfactual dependence is always necessary or sufficient

central_findings.finding: Explanation quality is relational, not an intrinsic property of a paragraph.
central_findings.consequence: Target, foil, background, audience/purpose, relation type, and scope must be declared before audit.

central_findings.finding: Quality is a gated partial order, not a compensatory scalar score.
central_findings.consequence: Elegance, simplicity, breadth, or detail cannot compensate for false premises, an unwarranted bridge, or no vulnerability to rivals.

central_findings.finding: Explanatory warrants are plural but disciplined.
central_findings.consequence: Causal, mechanistic, statistical, mathematical, constitutive, and intentional accounts require different evidence; they are not interchangeable.

central_findings.finding: Counterfactual reach is a powerful depth test where meaningful, not a universal definition.
central_findings.consequence: Use interventions for causal claims, but allow production, grounding, constitution, constraint, or derivational consequences where ordinary but-for dependence fails.
Details are retained only when they affect the stated contrast, warrant, consequences, scope, or rival discrimination; omitted details need an irrelevance reason.
Different accounts may coexist for different contrasts or relation types; conflicting same-scope consequences must be tested as rivals.

relation_type_routes.causal: intervention/invariance, temporal direction, common-cause controls, production evidence, and redundancy handling
relation_type_routes.mechanistic: entities, activities, organization, start/finish conditions, perturbation or decomposition evidence
relation_type_routes.statistical: stable probabilistic relation, calibration, rival confounding controls, domain and sampling boundary; correlation alone is insufficient
relation_type_routes.mathematical_constraint: valid derivation, indispensability of the cited structure, direction or asymmetry, and impossibility/invariance consequences
relation_type_routes.constitutive_or_grounding: asymmetric composition, realization, entailment, or dependence warrant; do not force an intervention semantics
relation_type_routes.intentional_or_reason_based: agent's reasons, sensitivity to alternatives, background norms/information, and rival causal-only accounts

ordered_gates.pass_condition: Target, foil, purpose, background, and scope are explicit.
Premises and observations are sufficiently true/evidenced for the claim; derivations are internally valid.
The cited relation has the evidence and direction required by its declared type.
Included factors answer the stated contrast; important omissions and irrelevant additions are controlled.
The account supports new type-appropriate consequences beyond restating the target.
At least one strong rival, a discriminating consequence, and a failure condition are explicit.

contract.preference_rule: Preferences rank only explanations that pass the relevant gates; they cannot rescue a failed gate.

j_jump.definition: A J-jump is an auditable change in representation that reorganizes variables, relations, levels, or admissible contrasts and earns acceptance by retaining warranted successes, gaining new discriminating reach, and exposing itself to new failure conditions.

criteria.J1_representation_change: The proposal changes the map, not merely the wording or number of details.
criteria.J2_retention: Previously validated consequences are preserved as a special case, or their failure boundary is explicitly demonstrated.
criteria.J3_new_reach: The new representation resolves at least one prior anomaly, rival, or previously unanswerable contrast.
criteria.J4_compression_control: The jump removes assumptions or detail without losing the warranted consequences it claims to retain.
criteria.J5_rival_discrimination: It produces consequences that separate it from the strongest old and alternative representations.
criteria.J6_falsifiability_growth: It creates at least one new concrete way to fail.

j_jump.decision_rule: Call a proposal a J-jump candidate only if J1 is true and J2-J6 are explicit. Promote it to a surviving J-jump only after the relevant explanation-contract gates pass.
rejected_shortcuts: a model-generated idea with no retained-success map
j_jump.meno_j_architecture_change: Candidate generation supplies representation mutations. The Falsification Engine evaluates preservation, warranted reach, and added vulnerability; it does not equate generation with thinking.

limitations: The type routes are an engineering contract, not a settled metaphysics of every possible explanation.
Type classification can itself be contested, especially for mixed causal-constitutive or mathematical-empirical explanations.
Intentional and normative explanation need deeper treatment before the contract is used outside scientific/technical domains.
The source set is purposive rather than a systematic review, and several books/articles were available only through official summaries or selected argument access.
A human or AI benchmark is still needed to test whether the contract improves explanatory judgment and J-jump discovery in practice.

next_theory_stage.name: Adversarial J-Jump Casebook
next_theory_stage.purpose: Apply the frozen contract to historical and synthetic representation changes without numerical datasets.
next_theory_stage.success_condition: The contract must distinguish genuine representational jumps from mere relabeling, added detail, curve fitting, and retrospective storytelling while recording disputed cases rather than forcing unanimity.
